sec: Non-cirrhotic diseases: EHPVO vs NCPF table, PHTN note and images

items.q: Fill up the alternative names in the table header: NCPF / IPH / Hepatoportal ______ / Obliterative portal ______.
items.exp: Header: 'NCPF/IPH/Hepatoportal Sclerosis Obliterative portal venopathy)'. (Book p1035)

items.q: Row 'Outcome' (demographic) — match — 1) EHPVO 2) NCPF … A) 20–40 yr adult Asian male B) 3–8 yr child (m/c cause of UGI bleed in children)
items.exp: EHPVO: 3–8 yr child (m/c cause of UGI bleed in children); NCPF: 20–40 yr adult Asian male. (Book p1035)

items.q: Rows 'Involvement' and 'Cause' — match — 1) EHPVO 2) NCPF … A) 3rd order portal vein; E. coli / arsenic associations, hypervitaminosis A B) 1st order portal vein; umbilical sepsis > prothrombotic state
items.exp: EHPVO: 1st order portal vein, umbilical sepsis > prothrombotic state. NCPF: 3rd order portal vein, E. coli/arsenic, hypervitaminosis A. (Book p1035)

items.q: A 6-year-old presents with massive haematemesis and a massive spleen; blood counts show anaemia and thrombocytopenia. Per the table, what explains the cytopenias and which condition is this?
items.exp: EHPVO presentation: 'massive UGI bleed + massive spleen (hypersplenism) → Anemia, thrombocytopenia'. NCPF presents similarly but in 20–40 yr adults. (Book p1035)

items.q: Row 'Prognosis' — judge: I EHPVO prognosis is good with no risk for cirrhosis. II NCPF prognosis is good with negligible risk for cirrhosis.
items.exp: EHPVO: 'Good, with no risk for cirrhosis'; NCPF: 'Good, negligible risk for cirrhosis'. (Book p1035)

items.q: Row 'Investigations' — match — 1) EHPVO 2) NCPF … A) IOC Doppler; biopsy (gold standard) shows obliterative portal venopathy B) IOC CT; cavernoma appearance of collaterals
items.exp: EHPVO: IOC CT, cavernoma appearance of collaterals. NCPF: IOC Doppler, biopsy gold std — obliterative portal venopathy. (Book p1035)

items.q: Fill up (EHPVO complications): Stunted growth and portal ______ — compression of the biliary system by portal ______.
items.exp: 'Portal biliopathy : compression of biliary system by portal collaterals.' NCPF complications: '—'. (Book p1035)

items.q: What treatment is printed for EHPVO, and what is printed for NCPF?
opts: EHPVO: endoscopic variceal ligation / endoscopic sclerotherapy; NCPF: '—' (none printed)
EHPVO: TIPSS after failed angioplasty; NCPF: liver transplant (only treatment)
EHPVO: mandatory anticoagulation; NCPF: splenectomy with devascularisation
Both: angioplasty ± stenting, then endoscopic sclerotherapy on failure
items.exp: Treatment row: EHPVO = Endoscopic variceal ligation / Endoscopic sclerotherapy; NCPF = '—'. (Book p1035)

items.q: Note on the most common cause of portal hypertension — 1) Asia 2) World … A) Biliary atresia B) EHPVO
items.exp: 'm/c cause of PHTN : Asia: EHPVO; world: Biliary atresia.' (Book p1035)

items.q: Match — 1) CECT panels 2) Colour Doppler 3) Trichrome/H&E micrograph … A) Obliterative portal venopathy — sclerotic & non-patent portal tracts B) EHPVO showing collaterals C) EHPVO with cavernoma labelled
items.exp: 'CECT: EHPVO showing collaterals'; 'Color doppler : EHPVO' with 'Cavernoma' arrow; 'Obliterative portal venopathy' with 'Sclerotic & non patent portal tracts'. (Book p1035)
